title: Clarinetists of the 1920s and Georgie Boyd
summary: Barnes lists clarinet players in town in the 1920s including Jimbo, Johnny Dots, Pills, Zeb and Joe Watson, and calls George Boyd rougher than himself.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Who were some of the other clarinet players in town in the 20s?

Well I don't know. In the 20s I believe we had Art and Hale. Here we had Jimbo. Yeah Jimbo was out here in the 20s. Now here we had Johnny Hunnicall. Johnny Dots. Johnny Dots. We had Pills. And uh. Had this other boy Zeb. Had Zeb. Then this boy Joe Watson. Had him. And uh. Kaiser. We had Kaiser. We had Georgie boy.
What kind of a clarinet player was Georgie Boyd? John Boyd was a pretty good clarinet player. Would you say he had a rough style?

Well yeah his style was more rough than I was. Rougher than you? Yeah. He's a hard clarinet player. Was he strong? He's pretty strong. But I got to lean on all of them. I didn't ask for it or say I had it. They gave it to me. On Hale I didn't know. After I was playing a whole lot of clarinet. And that time. They had a good little clarinet play some of them boys. I can't remember. Who were the ones that you liked especially? In clarinet? Well the one I liked in clarinet really was uh. I say for instance you say like. In clarinet playing. Well I liked it George Brackey. I was crazy for George Brackey. I thought he was one of him and the big idol. Louie not to know what I mean dear
